front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from Ayat 41 in which the word Ankabut (Spider) is mentioned.

items.text: مَثَلُ الَّذِيۡنَ اتَّخَذُوۡا مِنۡ دُوۡنِ اللّٰهِ اَوۡلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ الۡعَنۡكَبُوۡتِ  اِتَّخَذَتۡ بَيۡتًا ؕ وَ اِنَّ اَوۡهَنَ الۡبُيُوۡتِ لَبَيۡتُ الۡعَنۡكَبُوۡتِ لَوۡ كَانُوۡا يَعۡلَمُوۡنَ
(29:41) The parable of those who take protectors other than Allah is that of a spider spinning a shelter. And the flimsiest of all shelters is certainly that of a spider, if only they knew.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is an early Makkan Surah before the migration to Ebyssinia. It has 69 Ayats in 7 rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
The Surah was revealed at a time of extreme persecution for the Muslims in Makkah. The disbelievers were forcefully opposing Islam and hence new converts were being subjected to the severest oppression. Such were the conditions when Allah SWT sent down this Surah to strengthen and encourage the sincere Muslims as well as to put to shame those who were showing weakness of the faith.

Questions that some young men asked regarding obeying parents were answered. For instance, parents were urging their children to abandon Muhammad (may Allah's peace be upon him), and return to their ancestral religion. They argued: "The Quran in which you have put your faith, regards the rights of the parents as the uppermost; therefore, listen to what we say; otherwise, you will be working against the dictates of your own Faith." This false logic has been answered in Ayat 8.

The stories mentioned in this Surah are meant to provide solace and courage for the believers while warn the disbelievers to cease and desist from the constant persecution. Then the Muslims have been instructed to the effect: "If you feel that the persecution has become unbearable for you, you should give up your homes, instead of giving up your Faith: Allah's earth is vast: seek a new place where you can worship Allah with the full peace of mind."

sections.title: 1-7 ALLAH TESTS THE BELIEVERS TO SEE WHO IS TRUTHFUL AND WHO IS A LIAR

arabic_lines: ۞  الٓمٓ

translation.text: Alif Lam Mim

arabic_lines: اَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ اَنۡ يُّتۡرَكُوۡۤا اَنۡ يَّقُوۡلُوۡۤا اٰمَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَـنُوۡنَ

translation.text: Do people think that they will be let go merely by saying: “We believe,” and that they will not be tested

commentary.text: The Believers are tested so that it may be known Who is Sincere and Who is Lying
This is a rebuke in the form of a question.

Context: The conditions prevailing in Makkah, at this time, were extremely trying for whoever accepted Islam as they were then made a target of humiliation and persecution. Allah SWT says that declaring Iman with your tongue is not enough. Thus, as soon as one proclaims Iman then life’s trials and tests begin. This is so as to sort out the believers from the non-believers/hypocrites. The result of bringing Quran in one’s life is that tests and trials commence however it is important to note that there is nothing but khair (good) in the tests for a believer as they help erase sins.

Who will be tested? Prophets, then the righteous, then those who do good, etc. etc. Thus, tests are in accordance and in correlation to one’s level of Iman/faith. The higher one's Iman the greater the test.

Misconception being refuted here that don’t assume that because you said you believe your life now becomes easy. That is, we expect ease and comfort for being good and declaring our faith but Allah SWT says now tests will be part of your life. Heaven is not attained by mere lip service but by actions and sincerity. Allah SWT constantly tests the faith of believers and the hypocrites so that whatever is hidden in their hearts is exposed and the truth is manifest/clear.
In Makki Quran this Surah is the root that then sprouts the following similar surahs. Surah Baqara Ayat 214, Surah Imran, and Surah Tawba Ayat 16.
Note: Repentance and giving charity helps alleviate trails and difficulties.

arabic_lines: وَمَنۡ جَاهَدَ فَاِنَّمَا يُجَاهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهٖؕ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ لَـغَنِىٌّ عَنِ الۡعٰلَمِيۡنَ

translation.text: Whosoever strives (in the cause of Allah) does so to his own good. Surely Allah stands in no need of anyone in the whole Universe

commentary.text: To be clear: Allah SWT is not asking us to exert our utmost because He needs help to establish His Godhead rather, He instructs you to enter this struggle as it opens the path to salvation. Thus, by waging this war one will not do any favor to Allah SWT but will certainly help ourselves.
This struggle is real.

The word “mujahadah” means to strive, struggle and exert one’s utmost against an opponent. The struggle of a believer similar as he has to fight against Satan, who constantly frightens him regarding possible losses that one has to incur for the sake of good and allures him with the benefits and pleasures of the evil.
A believer also has to fight against his own desires/fancies/whims.
A believer also has to fight against, trends, morality, customs, way of life and social and economic principles that may be in conflict with his faith.
And the list goes on…..
The struggle is not of a day or two, but of an entire lifetime, of every moment of the day and night. And it is not a struggle in one field only but on every front of life.
This struggle is real.

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَحْسَنَ الَّذِي كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ

translation.text: As for those who believe and do good, We will certainly absolve them of their sins, and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.

commentary.text: Two results of the belief and righteous deeds have been mentioned: (1) That man’s evils deeds or sins will be wiped off; and (2) that he will be rewarded for the best of his deeds better than what he will actually deserves.
This point has been stated in other places in the Quran:
Surah Al-Anaam: Ayat 160: “He who will bring a good deed before Allah, will receive a tenfold reward for it”
Surah Al-Qasas: Ayat 4: “Whoever brings a good deed, shall have a better reward than that”
Surah An-Nisa: Ayat 40: “Indeed Allah does not wrong anyone even by a jot: if one does a good deed, He increases it manifold.”
DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + good deeds = Salvation

sections.title: 8-13 BE KIND TO YOUR PARENTS BUT DO NOT OBEY THEM IN THE MATTER OF SHIRK AND THOSE WHO SAY, "FOLLOW US WE WILL BEAR YOUR BURDEN," ARE LIARS

translation.text: We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they exert pressure on you to associate with Me in My Divinity any that you do not know (to be My associate), do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I shall let you know all that you have done.

commentary.text: The Command to be Good and Dutiful to Parents

Context: This Ayat was revealed in the matter of Saad bin Abi Waqqas – a young man who embraced Islam. When his mother, Hamnah, daughter of Sufyan bin Umayyah (neice of Abu Sufyan), came to know that her son had become a Muslim, she said, “I will neither eat nor drink nor sit in shade unless you disown Muhammad. The rights of the mother are superior even according to Allah’s command. Therefore, if you disobey me, you will be disobeying Allah too.”

Saad was perplexed and related his dilemma to the Prophet (PBUH). Then this Ayat was revealed. Possibly other young men who embraced Islam during the initial stages in Makkah were also confronted with similar situations. Therefore, the same theme has been repeated forcefully in (Surah Luqman: Ayat 15 below.)

(31:15) But if they press you to associate others with Me in My Divinity, (to associate) those regarding whom you have no knowledge (that they are My associates), do not obey them. And yet treat them well in this world, and follow the way of him who turns to Me in devotion. Eventually it is to Me that all of you shall return, and I shall then tell you all that you did.”
The rights of parents, among the creation of Allah SWT, are to be held as supreme however if one's parent's force you to adopt shirk, then they should not be obeyed.

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ لَـنُدۡخِلَـنَّهُمۡ فِى الصّٰلِحِيۡنَ

translation.text: Those who believe and do good will surely be admitted by Us into ˹the company of˺ the righteous.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + good deeds = Success

Embracing Iman, more often than not, means cutting off from your old relationships. But Allah SWT promises new/righteous company that revolves around one thing which is Iman. This promise of Allah SWT of the ‘company of the righteous..’ is for this world as well as the next.

Note: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) has been commanded twice – in Surah Hijir and TaHa – to be very soft, kind and gentle with his followers and those who have accepted Islam because those who accepted Islam had to endure considerable sacrifice including cutting off from their loved ones.

translation.text: There are some who say, “We believe in Allah,” but when they suffer in the cause of Allah, they mistake ˹this˺ persecution at the hands of people for the punishment of Allah. But when victory comes from your Lord, they surely say ˹to the believers˺, “We have always been with you.” Does Allah not know best what is in the hearts of all beings?

commentary.text: The Attitudes of the Hypocrites and the Ways in which Allah tests People

Allah SWT wants to differentiate between those who swing like a pendulum amidst Iman and disbelief depending upon circumstances meaning when the going gets tough they get going. Thus, here the characteristic of a hypocrite is made clear.
Note: Allah SWT will put you through difficulty (at times isolation from family and friends) so that you can attain the sweetness of iman.

arabic_lines: وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنَا ...

translation.text: Those who disbelieve say to the believers, ‘Follow our path and we shall bear [the consequences for] your sins,’ yet they will not do so––they are liars.

commentary.text: The Arrogant Claim of the Disbelievers that They would carry the Sins of Others if They would return to Disbelief

The assertion of the arrogant disbelievers is/was that they would/will carry the sins of others if only they returned to disbelief. Context: The disbelievers of Quraysh said to those who believed and followed the truth: "leave your religion, come back to our religion and follow our way; and if there is any sin on you, we will bear it and it will be our responsibility'.
They are in fact LIARS! It is like a person saying: "commit murder and I will take the blame for it.” At the time of punishment all promises are broken.

translation.text: Yet they will certainly ˹be made to˺ carry their own burdens, as well as other burdens along with their own. And they will surely be questioned on Judgment Day about what they used to fabricate.

commentary.text: Here Allah SWT tells us that on the Day of Resurrection those who call others to disbelief and misguidance will bear their own sins and the sins of those they misguided.
Conversely, those who call others to true guidance, will have a reward the same as those who follow him, until the Day of Resurrection, without it detracting from their reward in the slightest.

Hadith: A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with a mountain of good deeds but he had wronged many, for example, taken the wealth of someone, slandered the honor of another etc. So, each who is wronged is entitled to take from his good deeds. And if there is nothing left of his good deeds, it will be taken from their evil and placed on him.
Lesson:  Be exceedingly mindful when doling out advice and guidance.  Keep in mind the above principle.

The first 13 Ayats of this Surah should be the foundation/advice/guidance for anyone who wants to start an Islamic crusade or movement as it outlines the core issues that will arise including; how to handle persecution, understand that sacrifice is part and parcel of becoming a Muslim, how to motivate new converts, and what rewards await etc.

sections.title: 14-22 NUH ADMONISHED HIS PEOPLE NOT TO COMMIT SHIRK FOR 950 YEARS LIKEWISE, IBRAHIM ADMONISHED HIS PEOPLE NOT TO COMMIT SHIRK

intro.text: Here Allah SWT consoles His servant and Messenger Muhammad (PBUH) by narrating the account of Prophet Nuh (PBUH), who invited his nation to Islam for 950 years, night and day, in secret and openly, yet, they persisted in their aversion to the truth.

Allah SWT informs us of how His servant, Messenger and close friend Ibrahim, the Imam of the monotheists, called his people to worship Allah alone, to fear Him alone, to seek provision from Him alone, to give thanks to Him alone, for He is the One to Whom thanks should be given for the blessings which none can bestow but He.
Prophet after Prophet is mentioned so that we understand that with the affirmation of Iman difficulties/tests/trials begin.

arabic_lines: وَاِبۡرٰهِيۡمَ اِذۡ قَالَ لِقَوۡمِهِ اعۡبُدُوا اللّٰهَ وَاتَّقُوۡهُ ؕ ذٰ لِكُمۡ خَيۡرٌ لَّـكُمۡ اِنۡ كُنۡـتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُوۡنَ

translation.text: And ˹remember˺ when Ibrahim said to his people, “Worship Allah, and fear Him. This is better for you, if only you knew.

commentary.text: Ibrahim (PBUH) and all Prophets delivered the same message of faith to their nations.
Worship and (ii) Fear Allah SWT

translation.text: You worship besides Allah nothing but idols, simply creating lies ˹about them˺. Those you worship besides Allah certainly cannot give you any provision. So seek provision from Allah ˹alone˺, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.”

commentary.text: We are commanded to seek provision/substance from Allah SWT alone. Provision here doesn’t just mean a job or money rather the meaning is all encompassing i.e, children, spouse, relationships etc. Worship Allah SWT alone, and be grateful to Allah SWT alone.

Lesson: Understand that our purpose or objective in life is to worship/glorify Allah SWT so we should do what we were created to do and not dedicate our life to worshiping other things such as jobs, money, fame etc. Gain knowledge of Islam so that you can make the best decisions in life.

sections.title: 23-27 THE PEOPLE OF IBRAHIM EVEN TRIED TO BURN HIM ALIVE BUT ALLAH SAVED HIM AND LUT (HIS NEPHEW) IS THE ONLY ONE WHO AFFIRMED HIS BELIEF WITH HIM

translation.text: But the only response of Ibrahim’s people was to say: “Kill him or burn him!” But Allah saved him from the fire. Surely in this are signs for people who believe.

commentary.text: The Response of Ibrahim's People -- and how Allah SWT controlled the Fire
People plan and Allah plans!

They set ablaze a huge fire until its flames reached up to the sky. No greater fire had ever been lit. Then they threw Ibrahim (PBUH) into the fire. But Allah SWT cooled the fire making it safe. After spending several days in it, he emerged unscathed. Ibrahim (PBUH) offered his body to the flames, and he offered his son as a sacrifice, which is why he is beloved by the followers of all religions.

Lesson: Stop fearing people as an impediment towards fully accepting Islam, that is, ‘if I fully embrace Islam I might lose my job or friends etc’. Allah SWT alone provides and Allah SWT alone saves. But we must prove our sincerity.

translation.text: He said ˹to his people˺, “You have taken idols ˹for worship˺ instead of Allah, only to keep ˹the bond of˺ harmony among yourselves in this worldly life. But on the Day of Judgment you will disown and curse one another. Your home will be the Fire, and you will have no helper!”

commentary.text: That is, you have fashioned your life on the foundation of idol worship instead of God worship. This can keep you bound together in this world because any creed/belief, however wrong and ill conceived, can become a means of establishing mutual friendships, brotherhoods, and all other social, cultural, economic and political relationships.

However, this falsehood cannot endure in the Hereafter where only those relationships of love, friendship, cooperation, kinship and mutual regard will endure which have been based on the worship of One God and virtue/ piety in the world.

All relationships founded on disbelief, shirk and deviation will be severed, and all kinds of love will change into enmity and hatred. The son and the father, the husband and the wife, the saint and the disciple, all will curse each other, and each will blame his/her deviation on the other, and will say, “This wicked person led me astray so he/she should be given double punishment.”
This theme has been repeated in several places in the Quran:
Surah Az-Zukhruf (43:67): “Friends on that Day shall become enemies of one another, except the righteous.”

Surah Al- Aaraf (7:38) “As each generation will be entering Hell, it will curse its preceding generation till all generations shall be gathered together there; then each succeeding generation will say regarding the preceding one; O Lord, these were the people who led us astray; therefore, give them a double chastisement of the Fire,”

Surah Al- Ahzab (33:67-68): “And they will say; Our Lord, we obeyed our chiefs and our great men, and they led us astray from the right path. Lord, give them double chastisement and curse them severely.”
Lesson: What is the basis or foundation of choosing your relationships, friendships, spouses, work colleagues? If they are founded on Iman they will be eternal.

translation.text: We blessed him with Isaac and ˹later˺ Jacob, and reserved prophethood and revelation for his descendants. We gave him his reward in this life, and in the Hereafter he will certainly be among the righteous.

commentary.text: The Faith of Lut and His Emigration with Ibrahim
Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) chose to immigrate so that he could observe Iman without fear of persecution.

Allah SWT granted him happiness in this world that was connected to happiness in the Hereafter, for in this world he had plentiful provision, dutiful sons, a beautiful and righteous wife, and he was and still is spoken with high regard and honor.

Hadith: When a disbeliever performs a good deed they are rewarded in this world. When a believer performs a good deed there is a reward in this world and the next – although the better reward awaits in the next world.

Lesson: When we leave something for Allah SWT then Allah gives us better. In the case of Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) he received in this world family, prosperity and eternal good mention and in sha Allah greater reward of the Hereafter.

sections.title: 28-30 LUT WAS APPOINTED AS A RASOOL TOWARDS THE NATION OF HOMOSEXUALS

translation.text: And Lot: when He said to his people, ‘You practise outrageous acts that no people before you have ever committed.

What! Do you go to men (to satisfy your lust), engage in highway robbery, and commit evil deeds in your gatherings?” Then they had no answer to offer other than to say: “Bring Allah''s chastisement upon us if you are truthful.”

commentary.text: The preaching of Lut and what happened between Him and His People
Examples of Prophets begin again.

Allah SWT tells us that His Prophet Lut (PBUH) denounced his people for their evil deeds and their immoral actions, a deed which none of the sons of Adam had ever committed before them. Three crimes are mentioned: (i) Homosexuality (ii) Robbing and killing people (iii) Committing crimes with such open abandon that what is clearly wrong seems like it is right.
Lesson: Despite a wave of people going one way (the wrong way) do not stop or shy away from saying the right thing and giving dawah. Allah SWT will open doors and make things easy.

sections.title: 31-35 THEY REJECTED ALLAH'S GUIDANCE; AS A RESULT, ALLAH DESTROYED THEM ALL

intro.text: Allah SWT sent angels to help Prophet Lut (PBUH) against his nation of disbelievers. The punishment from Allah SWT was that He rained upon them hard baked stones of clay and turned the whole town upside down. The people were lifted up to the sky, then flung upside down upon the earth.

sections.title: 36-40 LIKEWISE THE NATIONS OF 'AD, THAMUD, MADYAN AND FIR'ON REJECTED THE RASOOLS OF ALLAH, WHICH RESULTED IN THEIR DESTRUCTION

translation.text: And `Ad and Thamud! And indeed (their destruction) is clearly apparent to you from their (ruined) dwellings. Shaytan made their foul deeds seem fair to them, and turned them away from the path, though they were intelligent.

commentary.text: The Destruction of Nations Who rejected Their Messengers
Allah SWT informs us about several nations of the past that disbelieved in their Messengers and how He destroyed them with a punishment befitting their crimes.

The people of Ad and Thamud were not ignorant and foolish people, in fact, they were the most civilized and intelligent people of their time. Therefore, it cannot be said that satan deluded them rather that they adopted the way shown by satan with open eyes and full understanding because it promised great pleasures and advantages; and they abandoned the way presented by the Prophets because it appeared to be colorless, tasteless and troublesome due to moral restrictions.

translation.text: [Remember] Qarun and Pharaoh and Haman: Moses brought them clear signs, but they behaved arrogantly on earth. They could not escape Us

commentary.text: Qarun, Pharon, his minister Haman and their troops were all destroyed due to their hunger for power, greed for money, arrogance and for instigating corruption on earth. Thus, their punishment was that they were submerged or swallowed into the earth by drowning (in the case of Pharon and his followers) or by being literally consumed up by the earth (in the case of Qaurn).

translation.text: And We punished each one of them for their sins: some We struck with a violent storm; some were overcome by a sudden blast; some We made the earth swallow; and some We drowned. It was not God who wronged them; they wronged themselves.

commentary.text: Lesson: Allah SWT’s rule: When we transgress punishment is an inevitability/certainty.

sections.title: 41-44 PARABLE OF THOSE WHO TAKE PROTECTORS OTHER THAN ALLAH

arabic_lines: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاء كَمَثَلِ الْعَنكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ الْعَنكَبُوتِ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ

translation.text: The parable of those who seek protectors from other than Allah is that of a spider who builds a house; but indeed, the weakest of houses is the spider's house -- if they but knew.

commentary.text: The likening of the false gods of the Idolators to the House of a Spider
All the above-mentioned nations were involved in shirk, and they worshipped and called upon deities/false gods as their helpers, guardians, who have the power to make or mar their destinies.
Ankabut (عَنكَبُوتِ ) in Arabic means spider. Among all the known types of nests, dens and other abodes of animals, the spider's web is the weakest. Even a mild breeze can break its threads.

After relating these events, Allah SWT is now warning the mushriks (and by default all of us): ‘The fact that you put your faith and trust in imaginary deities, i.e. idols, money, fame, pirs/saints, etc., instead of relying solely on Allah SWT, is like grasping onto a spider’s cobweb which cannot withstand even the slightest incumbrance/load.

Lesson: There Is no God but Allah SWT. When in despair, or need then rely only on Allah SWT. For when we reach out to anything else it is like reaching out to a spider’s web (the weakest of all houses).  Allah is offering His hand in friendship to us then why do we become friends with others?

arabic_lines: الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ وَمَا يَعْقِلُهَا إِلَّا الْعَالِمُونَ وَتِلْكَ

translation.text: These are the parables We set forth for humanity, but none will understand them except the people of knowledge.

commentary.text: If only people understood then they would never take any protector besides Allah SWT.  But few understand, reflect or take a deep dive into knowledge.
Lesson: This is a challenge from Allah SWT to reflect upon the parables found in the Quran so as to full comprehend what is being conveyed.

translation.text: Allah created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. Surely in this is a sign for the people of faith.

commentary.text: Allah SWT has created every single thing for and with a purpose. What is your goal or purpose in life?
